---
title: "Expected Value of the Exponential Term"
format: html
---

Assume

$$
\phi_r \stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim} N(0,1).
$$

Define

$$
Q=\sum_{\ell=k+1}^{m}\kappa_\ell
$$

and

$$
A=kS_0+\sum_{\ell=k+1}^{m}S_{\kappa_\ell}.
$$

We want

$$
E\left[
\exp\left\{
-\left(\mu-\frac{\sigma^2}{2}\right)\Delta t\,Q
+\sigma\sqrt{\Delta t}\,A
\right\}
\right].
$$

Since $Q$ is nonrandom,

$$
E[\cdots]
=
\exp\left\{
-\left(\mu-\frac{\sigma^2}{2}\right)\Delta t\,Q
\right\}
E\left[e^{\sigma\sqrt{\Delta t}A}\right].
$$

# Rewrite $A$ using independent increments

Recall

$$
S_i=\sum_{r=i}^{n-1}\phi_r.
$$

Thus, for $a\le b$,

$$
S_a-S_b=\sum_{r=a}^{b-1}\phi_r,
$$

and $S_n=0$.

Given

$$
0\le\kappa_{k+1}\le\kappa_{k+2}\le\cdots\le\kappa_m\le n,
$$

define

$$
\kappa_{m+1}=n.
$$

Then

$$
A
=
k\left(S_0-S_{\kappa_{k+1}}\right)
+
\sum_{i=k+1}^{m}
i\left(S_{\kappa_i}-S_{\kappa_{i+1}}\right).
$$

Expanding the right side gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
&kS_0-kS_{\kappa_{k+1}}\\
&\quad +(k+1)S_{\kappa_{k+1}}-(k+1)S_{\kappa_{k+2}}\\
&\quad +(k+2)S_{\kappa_{k+2}}-(k+2)S_{\kappa_{k+3}}\\
&\quad +\cdots\\
&\quad +mS_{\kappa_m}-mS_{\kappa_{m+1}}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Since $S_{\kappa_{m+1}}=S_n=0$, this reduces to

$$
kS_0+\sum_{\ell=k+1}^{m}S_{\kappa_\ell}=A.
$$

Using the definition of $S_i$,

$$
A
=
k\sum_{r=0}^{\kappa_{k+1}-1}\phi_r
+
\sum_{i=k+1}^{m}
i\sum_{r=\kappa_i}^{\kappa_{i+1}-1}\phi_r.
$$

The ranges of $r$ are disjoint. Since the $\phi_r$ are IID standard Gaussian variables, the sums are independent Gaussian variables.

In particular,

$$
\sum_{r=0}^{\kappa_{k+1}-1}\phi_r
\sim N(0,\kappa_{k+1}),
$$

and

$$
\sum_{r=\kappa_i}^{\kappa_{i+1}-1}\phi_r
\sim
N\left(0,\kappa_{i+1}-\kappa_i\right).
$$

Therefore

$$
A\sim N(0,V),
$$

where

$$
V
=
k^2\kappa_{k+1}
+
\sum_{i=k+1}^{m-1}
i^2(\kappa_{i+1}-\kappa_i)
+
m^2(n-\kappa_m).
$$

# Apply the Gaussian moment-generating function

For $Z\sim N(0,V)$,

$$
E[e^{tZ}]=e^{t^2V/2}.
$$

Taking

$$
t=\sigma\sqrt{\Delta t}
$$

gives

$$
E\left[e^{\sigma\sqrt{\Delta t}A}\right]
=
\exp\left\{
\frac{\sigma^2\Delta t}{2}V
\right\}.
$$

Hence

$$
\begin{aligned}
&E\left[
\exp\left\{
-\left(\mu-\frac{\sigma^2}{2}\right)\Delta t
\sum_{\ell=k+1}^{m}\kappa_\ell
+
\sigma\sqrt{\Delta t}
\left(
kS_0+\sum_{\ell=k+1}^{m}S_{\kappa_\ell}
\right)
\right\}
\right]\\
&=
\exp\left\{
-\left(\mu-\frac{\sigma^2}{2}\right)\Delta t
\sum_{\ell=k+1}^{m}\kappa_\ell
+
\frac{\sigma^2\Delta t}{2}
\left[
k^2\kappa_{k+1}
+
\sum_{i=k+1}^{m-1}i^2(\kappa_{i+1}-\kappa_i)
+
m^2(n-\kappa_m)
\right]
\right\}.
\end{aligned}
$$

# Simplify the variance

Starting with

$$
V
=
k^2\kappa_{k+1}
+
\sum_{i=k+1}^{m-1}i^2(\kappa_{i+1}-\kappa_i)
+
m^2(n-\kappa_m),
$$

expand the differences,

$$
\begin{aligned}
V
={}&k^2\kappa_{k+1}
+\sum_{i=k+1}^{m-1}i^2\kappa_{i+1}
-\sum_{i=k+1}^{m-1}i^2\kappa_i\\
&+m^2n-m^2\kappa_m.
\end{aligned}
$$

Collecting the coefficient of each $\kappa_\ell$ gives

$$
V
=
m^2n-\sum_{\ell=k+1}^{m}(2\ell-1)\kappa_\ell.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}
&E\left[
\exp\left\{
-\left(\mu-\frac{\sigma^2}{2}\right)\Delta t
\sum_{\ell=k+1}^{m}\kappa_\ell
+
\sigma\sqrt{\Delta t}
\left(
kS_0+\sum_{\ell=k+1}^{m}S_{\kappa_\ell}
\right)
\right\}
\right]\\
&=
\exp\left\{
-\left(\mu-\frac{\sigma^2}{2}\right)\Delta t
\sum_{\ell=k+1}^{m}\kappa_\ell
+
\frac{\sigma^2\Delta t}{2}
\left[
m^2n-\sum_{\ell=k+1}^{m}(2\ell-1)\kappa_\ell
\right]
\right\}.
\end{aligned}
$$

# Final simplification

Since

$$
-\left(\mu-\frac{\sigma^2}{2}\right)\Delta t
\sum_{\ell=k+1}^{m}\kappa_\ell
=
-\mu\Delta t\sum_{\ell=k+1}^{m}\kappa_\ell
+
\frac{\sigma^2\Delta t}{2}
\sum_{\ell=k+1}^{m}\kappa_\ell,
$$

combining the $\sigma^2$ terms gives

$$
\frac{\sigma^2\Delta t}{2}
\sum_{\ell=k+1}^{m}\kappa_\ell
-
\frac{\sigma^2\Delta t}{2}
\sum_{\ell=k+1}^{m}(2\ell-1)\kappa_\ell
=
-\sigma^2\Delta t
\sum_{\ell=k+1}^{m}(\ell-1)\kappa_\ell.
$$

Thus the final result is

$$
\begin{aligned}
&E\left[
\exp\left\{
-\left(\mu-\frac{\sigma^2}{2}\right)\Delta t
\sum_{\ell=k+1}^{m}\kappa_\ell
+
\sigma\sqrt{\Delta t}
\left(
kS_0+\sum_{\ell=k+1}^{m}S_{\kappa_\ell}
\right)
\right\}
\right]\\
&=
\exp\left\{
-\mu\Delta t
\sum_{\ell=k+1}^{m}\kappa_\ell
+
\frac{\sigma^2\Delta t}{2}m^2n
-
\sigma^2\Delta t
\sum_{\ell=k+1}^{m}(\ell-1)\kappa_\ell
\right\}.
\end{aligned}
$$
